```{r eval=TRUE, error=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=TRUE}

library("dplyr")
library("Seurat")
library("knitr")
library("ggplot2")
library("BiocManager")
library("here")
#BiocManager::install("EnhancedVolcano")
library("EnhancedVolcano") #volcano plot
#install.packages('DESeq2') #for DEG
library("DESeq2")
library("tidyverse") #tidy up data
library("styler") #tidy up data
library("scCustomize") #for color scales)


if (!require("kableExtra")) {install.packages("kableExtra"); require("kableExtra")} # for color brewer
if (!require("RColorBrewer")) {install.packages("RColorBrewer"); require("RColorBrewer")} # for color brewer
if (!require("sctransform")) {install.packages("sctransform"); require("sctransform")} # for data normalization
if (!require("glmGamPoi")) {BiocManager::install('glmGamPoi'); require("glmGamPoi")} # for data normalization, sctransform
if (!require("cowplot")) {install.packages("cowplot"); require("cowplot")} # for figure layout
if (!require("patchwork")) {install.packages("patchwork"); require("patchwork")} # for figure patching
if (!require("openxlsx")) {install.packages("openxlsx"); require("openxlsx")} # to save .xlsx files

# install.packages("styler")



set.seed(12345)
# here()

```

# Welcome

![](`r here::here("Week 3 Reporting Findings", "Images", "Welcome.png")`)

Welcome to the **Single-Cell Omics Research and Education Club**!

If this is your time to the club, **I want to extend and extra-special welcome to you!**

I'm **Jonathan Nelson**, an Assistant Professor at the University of Southern California. I'm a **wet** scientist turned **wet+dry** scientist. I've been working with **single-cell RNAseq data** for the past **5 years** and I'm excited to share what I've learned with you.

## SCORE Values

### **Learning**
We believe that bioinformatics is a constantly evolving field, and that ongoing learning and professional development is essential to staying up-to-date. We encourage members to share their knowledge and experiences with each other, and to seek out opportunities for continued learning.

### **Accessibility**
We believe that access to bioinformatics support should be available to everyone. We strive to create a welcoming and inclusive environment where all members can feel comfortable asking for help and contributing to the group.

### **Collaboration**
We believe that working together is key to achieving success in bioinformatics. We value the diversity of perspectives and backgrounds that each member brings, and we encourage open communication and the sharing of ideas.

### **Integrity**
We believe in conducting ourselves with honesty and professionalism in all our interactions. We hold ourselves to high ethical standards and respect the privacy and confidentiality of all members.

### **Empathy**
We believe in approaching each other with empathy and kindness. We understand that bioinformatics can be a challenging and sometimes frustrating field, and we strive to support each other through these difficulties.

## It **finally** happened!

### I got too tired of **switching** between my Seurat v4 and Seurat v5 computers

![](`r here::here("Week 5 KPMP snRNaseq", "Images", "Week 5","btf.webp")`)

#### Screenshot from **Score #1**

## What is renv?

![](`r here::here("Week 5 KPMP snRNaseq", "Images", "Week 5","renv_logo.png")`)

https://rstudio.github.io/renv/articles/renv.html

### A package for managing R project environments

### Let's be honest...we often get stuck in between projects as packages change

![](`r here::here("Week 5 KPMP snRNaseq", "Images", "Week 5","renv_image.svg")`)

### It allows you to create a **snapshot** of your R packages and versions

![](`r here::here("Week 5 KPMP snRNaseq", "Images", "Week 5","renv_graphic.png")`)

### It allows you to **restore** your R packages and versions

![](`r here::here("Week 5 KPMP snRNaseq", "Images", "Week 5","renv_files.png")`)

### **Great** video from **Albert Rapp** on using renv 

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Oen9xhEh8PY

![](`r here::here("Week 5 KPMP snRNaseq", "Images", "Week 5","youtube.jpg")`)

### It took me **5 minutes** to set this up on my system

### I started by using the *renv* package in a new github repo that I was working on

### **This easy!**

#### Open up project from the folder where you want to use renv

![](`r here::here("Week 5 KPMP snRNaseq", "Images", "Week 5","thiseasy.png")`)

![](`r here::here("Week 5 KPMP snRNaseq", "Images", "Week 5","filesize.png")`)

### Now when I open the project from this location:  **Seurat v5**

### When I open project from any other folder: **Seurat v4**

## **Take Home**

### Implimenting *renv* is a great way to manage your R packages and versions
### It's been seamless and helped me to move between **Seurat v4** and **Seurat v5**
### Important for making your code **reproducible!**
#### Add a renv.lock file to your git repo so that others can use the same packages and versions

## Start with a Seurat Object

### Data from Figure 1 from Burfeind et al. Phys Genomics 2025

https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39982410/

![](`r here::here("Week 5 KPMP snRNaseq", "Images", "Week 5","burfiend.png")`)

### Load Dataset

```{r eval=FALSE, error=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=TRUE}

SO <- readRDS(here("Week 4 CellChat", "data", "CACPR_integrated.rds"))

DimPlot(SO, group.by = "subclass.CACPR") + ggtitle("")

DefaultAssay(SO) <- "RNA"

SO@meta.data

```

![](`r here::here("Week 5 KPMP snRNaseq", "Images", "Week 5","dimplot.png")`)

### Step 1: Create a list of genes

```{r eval=FALSE, error=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=TRUE, fig.width=10, fig.height=8}

markers.to.plot1 <- c("Lrp2",         # PT
                      "Slc5a12",      # PT-S1
                      "Slc13a3",      # PT-S2
                      "Slc16a9",      # PT-S3
                      "Havcr1",       # Injured PT
                      "Epha7",        # dTL
                      "Slc12a1",      # TAL
                      "Cldn10",       # TAL
                      "Cldn16",       # TAL
                      "Nos1",         # MD
                      "Slc12a3",      # DCT
                      "Pvalb",        # DCT1
                      "Slc8a1",       # DCT2, CNT
                      "Aqp2",         # PC
                      "Slc4a1",       # IC-A
                      "Slc26a4",      # IC-B
                      "Upk1b",        # Uro
                      "Ncam1",        # PEC
                      "Pdgfrb",       # Perivascular
                      "Piezo2",       # Mesangial
                      "Pdgfra",       # Fib
                      "Acta2",        # Mural
                      "Nphs1",        # Podo
                      "Kdr",          # Capillary Endo
                      "Lyve1",        # Lymph
                      "Ptprc",        # Immune
                      "Cd74",         # Macrophage
                      "Skap1"         # B/T Cells 
                      )

```

### Step 1b: Multidimentional Dotplot code

```{r eval=FALSE, error=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=TRUE, fig.width=10, fig.height=8}

DotPlot(SO,
features = markers.to.plot1,
dot.scale = 8,
dot.min = 0,
scale.max = 100,
scale.min = 0,
col.min = -2.5,
col.max = 2.5,
group.by = "class.CACPR") +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(axis.line = element_line(size = 1, colour = "black"),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
        panel.border = element_blank(),
        panel.background = element_blank(),
        text = element_text(size=20),
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  xlab(NULL) +
  ylab(NULL)

```

### Step 2: Violin Plot of List in Features

```{r eval=FALSE, error=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=TRUE, fig.width=20, fig.height=20}
VlnPlot(SO,
features = markers.to.plot1,
group.by = "subclass.CACPR")

```

![](`r here::here("Week 5 KPMP snRNaseq", "Images", "Week 5","vlnplots.png")`)

#### Looks really bad!

### Step 3: Change the `stack =` argument

#### **?VlnPlot**
#### Gives you the modifiable arguements in the Vln Function

![](`r here::here("Week 5 KPMP snRNaseq", "Images", "Week 5","vlnplot.png")`)

```{r eval=FALSE, error=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=TRUE, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}

VlnPlot(SO,
features = markers.to.plot1,
group.by = "subclass.CACPR",
stack = TRUE)  # This is the key argument to change

```

![](`r here::here("Week 5 KPMP snRNaseq", "Images", "Week 5","stacked.png")`)

### Sometimes creating graphs is as sample as knowing the *arguments* in a function

## snRNAseq object: WashU-UCSD_HuBMAP_KPMP-Biopsy_10X-R_12032021.h5Seurat

### Code to load

```{r eval=FALSE, error=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=TRUE}

if (!require("SeuratDisk")) {install.packages("SeuratDisk"); require("SeuratDisk")}

SO <- LoadH5Seurat(here("WashU-UCSD_HuBMAP_KPMP-Biopsy_10X-R_12032021.h5Seurat"))

```

### Notes

#### This is **Atlas 1.0** data
#### Newer files have **more samples**...but are a **smaller file** size because it's filtered more
#### When publishing...make sure to define the **file** you used
#### KPMP is **consistently updating** files with more samples
#### Goals is to have **1000 participants**
